p4-w25-m2.alt: A hand-drawn whiteboard in three bands: an embedding matrix of 128,256 rows by 4,096 columns with row 9,514 highlighted and an arrow taking it out as a single 4,096-wide vector strip labelled LOOKUP; four stacked token strips labelled with the tensor shape beside a crossed-out shuffled copy showing that a set has no order, with two fixes drawn side by side - adding a sinusoidal wave for absolute position and rotating the vector by m times theta for RoPE; and a bar chart of Llama-3-8B KV-cache size at 8k, 32k and 128k context reaching 1, 4 and 16 GiB against a red line marking the 7.9 GiB left on a 24 GB card.

p4-w25-m3.title: One attention row, worked out by hand
p4-w25-m3.alt: A hand-drawn whiteboard showing the sentence 'the tired cat slept' with query, key and value strips hachured under each word, a four-by-four attention grid whose upper triangle is dashed red and crossed out as minus infinity before softmax, the bottom row filled in with 0.077, 0.082, 0.650 and 0.191 and the 0.650 highlighted, the exponentials and their sum of 13.03 left visible as rough work beside it, the scale factor root 128 equals 11.31 in its own panel, and three attention matrices drawn to the same scale where the 128k square dwarfs the nested 8k and 1k squares.

p4-w25-m4.title: The block: one highway, two deposits
p4-w25-m4.alt: A hand-drawn whiteboard showing a thick vertical residual stream labelled (B, T, 4096) with two side branches rejoining it through plus symbols - a narrow attention branch of 41.9 million parameters preceded by an RMSNorm, and a much wider feed-forward branch of gate, up and down projections between 4096 and 14336 totalling 176.2 million - with a crossed-out post-norm alternative at the left, two bars showing the feed-forward network is 81 percent of every layer, and the running arithmetic 218.1M times 32 plus two 525M embedding tables reaching 8.03 billion parameters.

p4-w25-m5.title: Prefill is fat and short. Decode is thin and long.
p4-w25-m5.alt: A hand-drawn whiteboard whose top band is a single timeline: prefill is one dense block occupying about a ninetieth of it at 0.27 seconds for 1,024 prompt tokens, and decode is a long row of sixty small separate boxes stretching across the rest at 25 seconds for 1,024 generated tokens. Below, the per-token KV-cache formula is written out longhand reaching 512 KiB per token, with a staircase of slabs growing under the decode row and running totals of 2 GiB at 4k and 4 GiB at 8k, beside a crossed-out no-cache loop at 3.2 tokens per second. At the bottom a roofline plot marks the ridge at 208 FLOPs per byte with decode sitting far down the ramp at 2 and prefill on the ceiling at 2,048.

p4-w26-m1.title: Fewer bits = a coarser grid, and the outliers pay
p4-w26-m1.alt: A hand-drawn whiteboard: four bit-strips drawn to scale for fp32, bf16, fp16 and int8 with the value 0.1 stored in each and its error written beside it; two number lines showing a weight snapping to the nearest representable value, tiny for fp16 and ten times larger for int4's sixteen levels; a weight-magnitude histogram whose narrow bell is followed by three circled outlier crosses far to the right labelled 0.1% of dimensions up to 20x larger; a crossed-out naive int8 box beside a ticked LLM.int8() box; and a Pareto scatter of GGUF quantizations from q2_K at 3.18 GB scoring 27 out of 50 up to q8_0 at 8.54 GB scoring 43, with the knee highlighted at q4_K_M.

p4-w26-m2.title: Fine-tune or not: walk the tree, do not argue
p4-w26-m2.alt: A hand-drawn decision tree. The root asks whether the model is missing facts or missing behaviour. The facts branch runs left through putting it in the prompt and then RAG to a green terminal costing two days and $0.0006 a query, with the branch from facts to fine-tuning crossed out in red and two bars beneath showing 31 percent recall from fine-tuning against 94 percent from putting the same facts in the prompt. The behaviour branch runs right through better prompts, five-shot examples and a hundred-item eval before reaching fine-tuning, beside memory bars of 132.6, 21.3 and 14.2 GB for full fine-tuning, LoRA and QLoRA against a dashed 24 GB A10G line.

p4-w26-m3.title: LoRA: 256 times fewer, and you can see it
p4-w26-m3.alt: A hand-drawn whiteboard in which a densely hachured 4096 by 4096 square marked FROZEN with a padlock holds 16,777,216 parameters, while the LoRA detour beneath it is two slivers so thin they are drawn eight times thicker than true scale, meeting at a rank-eight waist and rejoining through a plus, with the arithmetic 32,768 plus 32,768 equals 65,536 and the ratio 256 circled. Below, a decaying singular-value spectrum recalls week 11, three bars compare 132.6, 21.3 and 14.2 GB against a 24 GB A10G line, and eight crossed-out full model copies are replaced by one base model with eight small adapter tabs clipped on.

p4-w26-m4.title: Constrained decoding masks logits, not meaning
p4-w26-m4.alt: A hand-drawn whiteboard with a seven-state JSON state machine drawn as a chain from START to DONE with EXPECT_COLON highlighted as the current state, a bar chart of thirty vocabulary logits in which all but three are struck through in red and dropped to a hand-drawn minus-infinity floor while the colon, colon-space and whitespace tokens survive, two panels contrasting guaranteed syntax against unchanged F1 of 0.74, the claim that constrained decoding improves quality crossed out and corrected to parseability, and a grouped bar chart where schema validity climbs from 58.5 to 100 percent while field F1 moves only from 0.61 to 0.74.

p4-w26-m5.title: Continuous batching, and the KV page table
p4-w26-m5.alt: A hand-drawn whiteboard with two eight-row request timelines: under static batching seven rows finish early and the rest of each row is dashed idle until a red barrier at the longest request, giving 402 tokens a second; under continuous batching new requests fill each row the moment it frees, giving 934. Below, the KV cache region is drawn twice - once with three sequences pre-allocated to max_model_len and most of each block hachured red as waste, struck through, and once as thirty small 16-token blocks allocated out of order with one amber block shared between two sequences - annotated as the week 9 page table. At the bottom a throughput curve rises and flattens while per-request tokens per second falls, crossing near concurrency 32.

p4-w27-m1.title: The whole RAG pipeline, and where it actually breaks
p4-w27-m1.alt: A hand-drawn left-to-right RAG pipeline of ten boxes from PDFs through PARSE, CHUNK, EMBED, INDEX, RETRIEVE, RERANK, PROMPT and GENERATE to ANSWER, with a red exclamation mark and a failure mode written above every stage and the PARSE box drawn oversized, heavily outlined and highlighted. Below, the same two-column page is shown twice: once with a red snaking arrow reading straight across both columns producing interleaved nonsense that is struck through, and once with the two columns detected and read separately producing readable text. A tally records 312 two-column, 41 scanned and 89 table-heavy documents out of a thousand, and two bars compare Recall@10 of 0.72 for naive parsing against 0.83 for layout-aware parsing.

p4-w27-m2.title: One document, split three ways
p4-w27-m2.alt: A hand-drawn whiteboard showing the same ruled document as four tall panels. At 128 tokens the highlighted answer passage is cut in half by a thick red line and Recall@10 is 0.71; at 2048 tokens the answer is a thin highlighted sliver inside one huge block, 0.74; at 512 tokens it sits wholly inside one chunk with amber 64-token overlap bands on every seam, 0.83; and a parent-child panel embeds four 256-token children that point up into a 1024-token parent. Below, an inverted-U curve plots Recall@10 of 0.71, 0.79, 0.83, 0.81 and 0.74 against chunk sizes 128 to 2048 with the peak at 512 ringed in green.

p4-w27-m3.title: Bi-encoder: the query and the document never meet
p4-w27-m3.alt: A hand-drawn whiteboard split down the middle. On the left a bi-encoder passes the query and the chunk through two copies of the same encoder that are separated by a red dashed line labelled THEY NEVER MEET, each producing a vector strip which meet only at a cosine circle giving 0.71, with a note that the document side is computed once at ingest - 47,300 chunks in 33 minutes - and is free at query time. On the right a cross-encoder takes one concatenated query-SEP-chunk input through a single model to 0.83, annotated in red that nothing can be precomputed and scoring the full corpus would take 43 seconds. Below, a scatter of chunk points around a query cross inside a dashed top-10 ring with two shaded as relevant, and four bars showing gte-large is 3.9 times slower for 0.005 more recall.

p4-w27-m4.title: HNSW is a skip list whose levels are graphs
p4-w27-m4.alt: A hand-drawn whiteboard with three stacked layers of a navigable small-world graph: a top layer holding 0.39 percent of nodes joined by three long hops, a middle layer with 6.25 percent, and a bottom layer containing every node, with dotted drop lines showing the same node exists in every layer below and a numbered six-step red search path descending greedily to the query cross. Beside it a crossed-out k-d tree square is annotated that in 768 dimensions it visits 94 percent of nodes, an inset shows the two heaps of the inner loop as the week-14 Dijkstra frontier, an IVF panel rings three of seven k-means centroids as nprobe equals three, and three bars compare ef_search 40 at recall 0.95 and 980 QPS against ef_search 10 and brute force.

p4-w27-m5.title: Attribute the failure before you fix anything
p4-w27-m5.alt: A hand-drawn diagnostic flowchart starting from 'the answer was WRONG' and branching first on whether the gold chunk reached the context window - 68 of 100 failures were retrieval - and then on whether it sat in the top five positions, splitting the rest into a position effect and 24 of 100 generation failures, with 8 both. To the right, a U-shaped curve plots answer accuracy 0.84, 0.71, 0.63, 0.68, 0.78 against the gold chunk's position in a twenty-chunk context with the dip at position ten ringed and labelled lost in the middle, and a bar chart shows accuracy peaking at k=10 with 0.81 and falling to 0.68 at k=50.

p4-w28-m1.title: BM25: rare terms carry the score
p4-w28-m1.alt: A hand-drawn whiteboard showing an inverted index whose common term 'return' has a posting list running off the page while 'ORA-01555' has exactly two postings, the BM25 formula written large with IDF underlined blue, the term-frequency numerator green and the saturating denominator amber, each labelled by hand. A saturation curve rises from 1.00 at one occurrence to only 2.17 at a hundred against a dashed ceiling of 2.2, four bars show one rare identifier with IDF 7.74 dwarfing 'error' and 'code' with the stopword struck out, and two result lists show dense retrieval putting the answer at rank 14 while BM25 puts it first, 0.39 against 0.94.

p4-w28-m2.title: RRF: the documents both retrievers found win
p4-w28-m2.alt: A hand-drawn whiteboard with three ranked columns. DENSE lists A B C D E and BM25 lists F C G A H, each entry annotated longhand with its reciprocal rank score from one over sixty-one downward. A and C, which appear in both lists, are ringed in amber and joined by curved arrows, and in the fused third column they rise to the top at .0320 each, above F at .0164 which was first in one list. An inset shows why the constant sixty flattens the gap between ranks one and two from 1.00-versus-0.50 to .0164-versus-.0161, two crossed-out score distributions show dense cosine and BM25 are not on the same scale, and a marginal-gain curve flattens after two retrievers at NDCG .790.

p4-w28-m3.title: Every rewrite is a generation you pay for first
p4-w28-m3.alt: A hand-drawn whiteboard in which a four-token query enters a red LLM box costing 420 milliseconds and fans out into two rewrites and a HyDE hypothetical answer, each hitting a dense and a BM25 retriever before merging through RRF to a top ten. Below, a scatter plots measured NDCG gain against added p50 latency for six techniques - rewrite at 180 ms for nothing, step-back 390, HyDE 420, multi-query 510, decomposition 780 - against a dashed 200 millisecond TTFT budget, with the router at 90 milliseconds highlighted for buying the same 0.02 gain. A crossed-out panel shows HyDE diluting the identifier query ORA-01555 from 0.93 to 0.66.

p4-w28-m4.title: Cheap over everything, expensive over fifty
p4-w28-m4.alt: A hand-drawn funnel: 47,300 chunks enter a wide mouth, pass through stage one hybrid retrieval at 8.9 milliseconds to a neck of 50 candidates, then through a stage two cross-encoder at 96 milliseconds to a spout of ten. Above, a bi-encoder sketch is labelled precomputed and free while a cross-encoder sketch must run per pair, and the margin arithmetic 47,300 pairs over 520 per second is circled as 91 SECONDS. Two ten-item result lists show the gold chunk moving from position seven to position one, and paired bars of NDCG and p95 latency by rerank depth 10 to 200 show quality flattening at 0.85 while latency climbs past a dashed 210 millisecond SLO line, with N=50 ringed as the knee.

p4-w28-m5.title: The cache threshold is a dial with a price on it
p4-w28-m5.alt: A hand-drawn similarity axis from 0.85 to 1.00 with the band above 0.97 hachured green as SERVE FROM CACHE and the rest blue as GO TO THE PIPELINE, annotated at four thresholds with hit rate and wrong-answer rate: 0.99 gives 38% and 0.3%, 0.97 gives 45% and 1.4% and is highlighted, 0.95 gives 53% and 4.9%, and 0.92 gives 61% and 13.2% and is struck through as one in eight answers wrong. Two nearly identical return-policy queries with cosine 0.961 but different answers show what a false hit is, a cost waterfall shows generation input tokens at $0.00046 of a $0.00065 query, a single-flight sketch coalesces 340 concurrent requests to one generation, and four unlabelled sparklines show the refusal rate stepping up first.

p4-w29-m1.title: An agent is a loop the model decides to leave
p4-w29-m1.alt: A hand-drawn whiteboard with three stacked panels: one call runs prompt to model to answer in a straight line, a chain runs through three model calls still in a straight line, and an agent is drawn as a genuine cycle from model to tool call to run it to observation and back, with a single dashed exit arrow labelled stop? and the word agent circled. A fourth panel reading 'just let it run until it's done' is struck through. To the right, a chart shows end-to-end success falling along the 95-percent-per-step curve from 95 at one step to 59.9 at ten - ringed with 0.95^10 = 0.60 written in - against a dashed 99-percent curve that reaches 90.4.

p4-w29-m1-curve.title: Reliability collapses with step count
p4-w29-m1-curve.alt: A hand-drawn chart of end-to-end agent success against the number of autonomous steps from one to twenty. Three declining curves show 90, 95 and 99 percent per-step reliability, reaching 34.9, 59.9 and 90.4 percent at ten steps, while a much flatter green curve for 95 percent with one verified retry - an effective 0.9975 - stays at 97.5 percent. A faint half-erased earlier attempt at the 95 percent curve is left visible underneath, an amber band covers steps one to four as where constrained workflows live, and an arrow labelled 'just add more steps' is struck through in red.

p4-w29-m2.title: One tool call is four messages on a wire
p4-w29-m2.alt: A hand-drawn sequence diagram between two lifelines, your process on the left and the model API on the right. Step one sends messages plus tool schemas, resent every turn and costing about 4,200 tokens for thirty tools. Step two returns a tool_use block with name, id and input. Step three is a self-loop on the left that validates arguments with Pydantic, runs the function and truncates the output, with a red ValidationError branch that returns the error as text rather than raising it into the void, which is drawn and struck through. Step four sends tool_result with a matching tool_use_id, annotated that a mismatch is a 400.

p4-w29-m3.title: The context window is a jar you refill every turn
p4-w29-m3.alt: A hand-drawn measuring jar labelled the context window, filled from the bottom with hachured token bands - system 900, tool schemas 4,200, rolling summary 350, last ten turns 4,500 and retrieved memories 600 - under a dashed red fill line, with a note that at 128k it still fits while recall has already fallen to 96 percent. The system and tool-schema bands are ringed in green as a cacheable prefix taking $1.60 to $0.20. A decision ellipse asks whether the fact will be needed by name later and routes to a pgvector STORE, a lossy SUMMARY or the verbatim WINDOW, while a box reading 'just send everything, context is 1M now' is struck through beside 613,750 tokens costing $3.34 for one fifty-turn chat.

p4-w29-m4.title: MCP collapses M x N - and draws a new red line
p4-w29-m4.alt: A hand-drawn two-panel diagram. On the left four hosts are wired to five services by twenty tangled red lines labelled M times N equals 20 integrations. On the right the same hosts and services each connect to one hachured green MCP bar, nine clean lines, M plus N equals 9, with a note that six assistants and twenty services go from 120 to 26. Beneath the right panel a heavy red dashed TRUST BOUNDARY separates the model from the filesystem, the database and a shell, and a thick red arrow labelled tool result crosses it upward, annotated that what comes back up is untrusted data the model cannot distinguish from an instruction. A shell tool implemented as subprocess.run with shell=True is struck through as RCE with a docstring, beside a green hardening box; fourteen lab attacks succeeded five times on v1 and zero times on v3.

p4-w29-m5.title: What the framework takes, and what you keep
p4-w29-m5.alt: A hand-drawn side-by-side comparison of the same nine agent-loop responsibilities. The left column, headed from scratch at 187 lines, shows all nine as plain boxes. The right column, headed Pydantic AI at 61 lines, shows seven of them hachured blue under a bracket labelled the framework owns this, while two remain yours and are outlined green: your tool functions and your output model. A red arrow points into the shaded region labelled 'you cannot see the exact bytes in here'. Underneath, six integration tests taking 214 seconds and $0.42 are struck through beside 34 tests in 1.9 seconds for nothing, and structured-output success rises from 89 to 98.5 percent with a validator retry.

p4-w30-m1.title: The line was a lie. It was always a graph.
p4-w30-m1.alt: A hand-drawn diagram in two halves. Above, a clean straight chain of triage, fetch logs, diagnose and report is struck through as what we wished it was. Below, the same work is redrawn as a graph with START and END nodes, a severity decision that routes P1 to a human, P2 and P3 to fetch logs and spam to END, and an 'enough evidence?' decision whose no branch is a real curved back-edge to fetch logs carrying a highlighted counter reading attempts 2 of max 3. A typed state card lists ticket_id, severity, log_excerpts as an appending list with reducer circled, attempts and hypothesis, with dashed lines to every node.

p4-w30-m2.title: Four multi-agent patterns, and what each cost
p4-w30-m2.alt: A hand-drawn two-by-two catalogue. Orchestrator-Specialist fans one box out to three specialists across a red dashed hand-off line and merges them back: 3.7x cost for plus 2.5 points, 77.5 percent at $0.71. Critic-Refiner loops write and critique around a rubric card: 1.8x for plus 7.5 points, 82.5 percent at $0.34, and it carries the only green tick on the page. Mixture of Agents runs the same task three times into an aggregate: 4.5x for plus 1.7. One strong agent with a self-loop is the 1.0x baseline at 75 percent and $0.19. Below, a shared-context sketch is struck through beside isolated 600-token briefs taking $0.71 down to $0.31.

p4-w30-m3.title: Resuming restores state. It replays effects.
p4-w30-m3.alt: A hand-drawn timeline of five nodes - triage, gather, diagnose, CHARGE and report - with a checkpoint cylinder after each completed node holding 3.2 KB of state, and a jagged red lightning bolt striking inside CHARGE labelled SIGTERM at 41 seconds. Below, a new process loads thread_id inc-4412 from the checkpoint before CHARGE and re-enters it, and two red arrows reach the bank: 240 pounds charged, then 240 pounds charged AGAIN, with the bank crossed out and 'this is the bug' written beside it. The fix is drawn in green: write an intent carrying a derived uuid5 idempotency key into an outbox queue, and let one worker be the only thing that touches money and dedupe on the key.

p4-w30-m4.title: Every failure leaf needs a named detector
p4-w30-m4.alt: A hand-drawn failure taxonomy rooted at 'run does not succeed, 6.5% of 4,200 runs', splitting into a thin blue LOUD branch and a heavy red SILENT branch. Loud leaves - tool timeout 2.1 percent, dependency down 0.3, malformed args 0.4 - each pair with a green detector box. Silent leaves - livelock 1.2 percent, budget exhaustion 0.9, step limit 0.26, contradictory instructions 0.2, confident wrong answer 1.1 - likewise, with livelock ringed and an inset showing three consecutive steps holding the identical three-dot evidence set. A four-bar gauge caps steps, tokens, dollars and wall-clock, and 'just raise max_steps' is struck through beside a runaway run of $18.40 capped to $0.50.

p4-w30-m5.title: One picture, one red line, three autonomy levels
p4-w30-m5.alt: A hand-drawn left-to-right incident-remediation architecture: TRIAGE, GATHER, DIAGNOSE, PROPOSE, then a heavy red dashed APPROVAL BOUNDARY, then EXECUTE, VERIFY and REPORT, each badged A for auto, S for suggest or H for human-approved. A bounded cycle runs back from DIAGNOSE to GATHER carrying attempts 2 of 3. Under GATHER sit the hybrid runbook corpus and an allow-listed audited MCP server; under EXECUTE sit three blast-radius cards - restart pod and scale deployment both reversible, and rotate credential marked IRREVERSIBLE and struck out as not in scope - plus a green rollback box. A hachured Postgres store of checkpoints and audit log sits beneath everything with dashed lines to every node.

p4-w31-m1.title: The eval pyramid: cheap at the bottom, true at the top
p4-w31-m1.alt: A hand-drawn four-band eval pyramid. The widest green base is deterministic assertions - format, length, entities, refusals, no PII - 120 cases in 0.8 seconds for nothing; above it reference matching on 40 cases for nothing; above that an LLM judge on 100 cases for $1.80 and 12 minutes; and at the narrow top human review of 20 cases weekly, the only ground truth. An arrow up the left is labelled cost per case and one down the right is labelled coverage. To the right a statistical-power curve shows the smallest detectable change falling from 24 points at 20 cases through 11 points at 100 - ringed - to 5 points at 500, and a box reading '20 hand-written cases we made up' is struck through beside a loop from a production failure into the pyramid's base.

p4-w31-m2.title: A judge is a classifier. Measure it first.
p4-w31-m2.alt: A hand-drawn diagram in which fifty outputs are scored independently by a human, the only ground truth, and by a rubric-driven judge, and both feed a two-by-two confusion matrix reading 28, 4, 3 and 15 that yields Cohen's kappa of 0.71 with po 0.86 and pe 0.52 written out. A thermometer beside it marks 0.0 coin flip through 0.6 SUBSTANTIAL, drawn as the green ship line, to 0.8 almost perfect. An arrow going straight from the judge to a CI gate, bypassing the matrix, is crossed out as the mistake everyone makes. Two insets show position bias - 61.5 percent picked whichever came first - and verbosity bias, the same content scoring 3.4 short and 4.0 padded, and three bars track kappa from 0.11 with no rubric to 0.71 with binary criteria and anchors.

p4-w31-m3.title: Four questions, four metrics, one culprit
p4-w31-m3.alt: A hand-drawn decision tree for a wrong RAG answer. Four question ellipses ask in turn whether the right document was retrieved (context RECALL, measured 0.91), whether most of what was retrieved was relevant (context PRECISION, 0.62), whether every claim is supported (FAITHFULNESS, 0.88) and whether the answer addresses the question (ANSWER RELEVANCY, 0.84); each no-branch lands on a named component - retrieval, re-ranking, generation hallucination, query transformation - and the final yes lands on 'the answer is right'. Beside it a five-node agent trajectory shows node 3 crossed out with a red arc back to a ringed node 1 labelled 'step 3 failed BECAUSE of step 1', with attribution 1 of 5 for end-state evaluation against 5 of 5 for trajectory evaluation.

p4-w31-m4.title: Only removing the capability reaches zero
p4-w31-m4.alt: A hand-drawn diagram: four differently-hachured input cards - trusted system prompt, semi-trusted user message, untrusted retrieved document and untrusted tool result - pour through a funnel into one uniform grey token stream, annotated that the model cannot see these colours and neither can you afterwards. A hostile IT NOTE hidden in the retrieved document is traced by a thick red path through the funnel and the model into the restart_service tool, labelled the confused deputy: your authority, their instruction. On the right, four amber barriers across the red path leak 33, 27 and 20 percent, while a much heavier green barrier with a padlock reads 'the tool is NOT in this agent's scope - 0% CATASTROPHIC'. A markdown image tag pointing at an attacker host is shown exfiltrating a secret off the page.

p4-w31-m5.title: Gates cost latency. Output gates cost streaming.
p4-w31-m5.alt: A hand-drawn request pipeline: user request, an input gate running Llama Guard 3 8B at plus 180 milliseconds to TTFT with TPR 0.81 and FPR 0.9 percent, the agent, then two output gates - PII redaction at plus 12 milliseconds and a groundedness check at plus 620 milliseconds - and finally the response. A heavy red bracket spans the two output gates labelled STREAMING IS DEAD HERE, noting TTFT goes from 0.9 to 4.1 seconds. Below, an ROC plot puts a crossed-out keyword filter at 0.11 false-positive rate and 0.41 true-positive rate, Llama Guard default at 0.04 and 0.89, and the tuned setting at 0.009 and 0.81 ringed in green just inside a dashed false-positive budget line at 0.01. A three-box guardrail layer sits on a much wider least-privilege foundation, and 'we added moderation, we're safe' is struck through.

p4-w32-m1.title: One run, one trace: duration AND cost on every bar
p4-w32-m1.alt: A hand-drawn distributed-trace waterfall inside a dashed box labelled trace_id. The root span agent.run incident.triage spans the full width at 34.1 seconds and $0.176. Five node spans nest inside it - triage 1.9 s $0.008, gather 11.4 s $0.031, diagnose 8.2 s $0.094, propose 6.1 s $0.039 and verify 5.9 s $0.004 - and three tool spans start together under gather, of which tool.read_runbook at 11.2 seconds is drawn much longer and marked in red as why gather is slow. A model-call span under diagnose carries 24,500 input and 1,920 output tokens, a running cost total ticks down the right edge to $0.176, and a print statement is struck through as unable to say what it was nested inside.

p4-w32-m2.title: The flywheel: a trace becomes a test becomes a fix
p4-w32-m2.alt: A hand-drawn, deliberately lopsided circle of five boxes with clockwise arrows: a production trace, an online score from a judge and user thumbs taken automatically in about 600 milliseconds, a labelled eval case created in four minutes where nine days is struck out, a versioned prompt v8 gated by the eval suite, and a deployment whose traces are tagged with the prompt version, closing back to production and verified there rather than only in CI. In the centre a small growth chart shows the eval suite going from 120 to 167 cases and the online score from 78 to 88 percent over eight weeks; below, a straight 'failure, fix, hope' arrow is struck through as no verification means no learning.

p4-w32-m3.title: Cheapest per call is not cheapest per task
p4-w32-m3.alt: A hand-drawn descending cost waterfall: a $0.190 baseline run falls through prompt caching minus $0.047, routing triage and verify to Haiku minus $0.015, evidence digests minus $0.024 and a semantic cache minus $0.028, then rises by $0.008 for verify-and-retry, ending at $0.084 a run - a 61 percent cut, with $0.253 and $0.098 per successful task boxed at either end. Beside it a scatter of cost per run against end-to-end success marks all-Haiku at $0.058 and 54 percent as $0.107 per success and therefore worse, the chosen configuration at $0.084 and 86 percent ringed in green as $0.098 per success, and the baseline at $0.190 and 75 percent, with a dashed Pareto frontier through the non-dominated points.

p4-w32-m4.title: TTFT is what the user feels. Detection is the incident.
p4-w32-m4.alt: A hand-drawn comparison of two timelines of identical total length: BUFFERED shows a flat grey bar labelled 'the user sees NOTHING - 4.00 s' ending in a burst, while STREAMED shows a 0.90 second prefill segment followed by a hachured region of words appearing that ends at the same 4-second mark, with a dashed amber line at 0.90 seconds marking TTFT. A small stacked bar breaks that 0.90 s into guardrail 180 ms, retrieval 210, queue 40 and model prefill 470. Below, an incident timeline runs from a provider model update through a scheduled eval detecting minus 6.2 points at 11 hours, pinning at 11 hours 20, root cause at 3 days and a fix at 4 days, with a crossed-out marker at 9 days reading 'a user tells us - this is the default', and a bracket over the first two markers labelled DETECTION.

p4-w32-m5.title: Eight weeks, one page, one deployable unit
p4-w32-m5.alt: A single-page hand-drawn architecture. A deploy lane across the top runs 5 percent canary, an eval gate, 25 percent, another gate and 100 percent, with red rollback arcs and a note that 3 of 14 rollouts stopped at a gate. The main flow runs from user or alert through an input guardrail costing 180 milliseconds, into an agent graph of six nodes with one cycle, then output checks for PII and groundedness, to the response. Beneath the graph sit pgvector hybrid RAG at recall@5 0.91 and Postgres checkpoints and audit log; to the right an MCP panel splits READ tools from three approval-gated WRITE verbs across a red trust boundary with a human at it. A dashed telemetry rail feeds OTel into Langfuse and an eval suite of 120 cases with judge kappa 0.71, which is the deploy gate. A heavy box at the top right holds five cards - code, prompts v8, pinned model, retrieval config and eval suite - that version together.
